sources.news_title: ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox News declined to replace CNN, leaving no television camera to cover Trump’s presidential events, the networks said.

Treasury Sec. Bessent, AI Control, & the White House Press Pool 9/21/26
Squawk Pod
Today
49 min
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is fresh off a meeting with China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng, just a few days before the meeting between President Trump and President Xi this week. Sec. Bessent shares takeaways from his own meeting, including his perspective on AI competition between the U.S. and China and the regulatory responsibility of AI developers. Plus, Sec. Bessent discusses the Federal Reserve’s latest rate hike and President Trump’s decision to revoke credentials from CNN, MS Now, and Politico journalists in the White House press pool. CNBC’s Eamon Javers reports on the joint lawsuit CNN, MS Now, and Politico filed against the Trump administration in response. In a discussion about AI safety and ethics, Stuart Russell, University of California at Berkeley professor and president of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI, considers the likelihood of maintaining control of AI as it grows more capable. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has dismissed many AI concerns as “doomsday narratives.”

By: Paul Goldberg – Senior Correspondent | LGBT Politics USA
WASHINGTON, D.C. — (September 21, 2026) — President Donald Trump’s decision to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House has escalated into a much larger confrontation with the American press — and the consequences became immediately visible, but barely audible, Monday.
Major television networks that normally rotate responsibility for providing independent pooled video and audio of presidential events suspended TV-pool coverage of Trump after CNN was prevented from taking its scheduled turn.

ABC News, CBS News, CNN, Fox News and NBC News joined together in the extraordinary action, putting normally competing — and politically diverse — television organizations on the same side of an escalating White House press-access dispute.
The result became strikingly apparent during Trump’s ribbon-cutting ceremony for the new South Lawn helipad.
The White House could provide its own video of the president, meaning viewers could see Trump speaking — but could barely hear what he was saying.
Without the normal television pool crew and its audio equipment, Trump’s remarks were overwhelmed by the sound of the nearby presidential helicopter. The Associated Press reported that whatever Trump said during the ceremony was impossible to hear over the aircraft noise.
For an administration attempting to restrict access by news organizations it considers hostile, the first major consequence was therefore an unusual one: the dispute interfered with the distribution of the president’s own message.
Fox, ABC, CBS and NBC Refuse to Replace CNN in Presidential TV Pool
CNN is one of five television networks — alongside ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox News — that rotate responsibility for providing pooled television coverage of presidential events.
When CNN was barred from fulfilling its scheduled pool assignment Monday, the other networks declined to replace it.
Bryan Boughton, Fox News’ Washington bureau chief and current chair of the White House television pool, informed the press corps that the pool would no longer cover events designated for presidential pool coverage.
Other pooled operations, including congressional and selected Washington coverage, were expected to continue normally.
The five television networks subsequently issued a joint statement defending independent coverage of the presidency.
“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government.”
They added:
“No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”
The involvement of Fox News is particularly notable because the network has frequently featured commentators and programming supportive of Trump. In this dispute, however, Fox joined its television-pool competitors in opposing the exclusion of CNN.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico Take Trump to Federal Court
The television networks’ action came as CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit Monday seeking restoration of their White House access.
Trump announced Friday that the three organizations would be barred, accusing them of publishing “FAKE NEWS.”
The organizations argue that the administration retaliated against them because of their journalism and therefore violated their First Amendment protections. Their complaint also raises Fifth Amendment due-process claims.
In their lawsuit, the three organizations described the ban as something that:
“could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles.”
A federal court hearing on their effort to regain access is expected this week.
The case adds another chapter to Trump’s long-running battles over White House press access. During his first administration, CNN correspondent Jim Acosta and Playboy reporter Brian Karem separately regained White House access after litigation challenging restrictions imposed on them.
Cable News Network, Inc. v. Trump
Case No. 1:26-cv-03287
U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia
Filed: September 21, 2026
Judge: Timothy J. Kelly
Even Trump-Friendly Media Figures Question the Ban
Criticism has not been confined to outlets typically viewed as hostile to Trump.
Former Trump White House press secretary Sean Spicer questioned the strategy while maintaining that he understood Trump’s objections to some news coverage.
“I don’t disagree with the president’s concern about some of these outlets, I just think there’s more effective ways to do this,”
Spicer told The Hill.
He also questioned the timing, arguing that the controversy overshadowed a White House announcement on prescription drug costs.
“And the other thing is the timing of this. On Friday he was having an amazing announcement on prescription drugs that gets to the affordability issue head on, and this obviously just stepped all over that,” Spicer said.
Right-leaning CNBC host Joe Kernen also challenged the administration’s approach while interviewing Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
“I just don’t think this is something we do in this country,”
Kernen said.
“You can’t control the press. The press is going to press, the media is going to media.”
Fox News commentator Brit Hume questioned what the president could gain from excluding the organizations, writing that:
“if he thinks this will lead to more favorable coverage, I think he’s dreaming.”
Those objections differ in their reasoning, but illustrate that opposition to the White House action has extended beyond Democratic politicians and media organizations generally critical of Trump.
White House Defends Decision to Block the Three Outlets
Trump has rejected accusations that his action constitutes an attack on press freedom.
In a Monday Truth Social post, the president insisted he is:
“not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish,”
and characterized his action instead as:
“an assault on the FAKE NEWS”
which he called a:
“threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”
A White House official similarly defended the restrictions, telling The Hill:
“Fake News has no place demanding a spot in the President’s Oval Office.”
The official added:
“The lies they smear are a disservice to the American public and tear at the very fabric of our Democracy. They’re completely capable of reporting from directly outside.”
The administration’s position is therefore that the outlets remain able to report on the presidency without being granted access to White House grounds. The plaintiffs contend that removing their credentials specifically because the administration objects to their reporting constitutes unconstitutional retaliation.
That disagreement is now before the federal courts.
White House Press Fight Suddenly Becomes an Audio Problem
Then came Monday’s South Lawn ceremony.
Trump appeared before cameras to inaugurate the White House’s newly constructed helipad. But with CNN unable to perform its scheduled pool duties and the other networks refusing to substitute for it, the normal independent television-pool operation wasn’t there.
The White House supplied video.
Usable pool audio was another matter.
Trump could be seen speaking during the ceremony, but the roar of the helicopter overwhelmed his remarks.
The problem was noticeable even at Newsmax.
As the right-leaning network attempted to cover the ceremony, anchor Bianca de la Garza acknowledged the consequences of the missing pool operation:
“So maybe this is one example of it backfiring just a little bit,”
She then summarized the problem facing viewers:
“Obviously the ramifications are right here … you can’t hear the president.”
Newsmax ultimately had the same basic technical problem confronting everyone else relying on the available feed: video of the president was available, but his remarks were drowned out.
The episode offered an unusually immediate demonstration of what the White House television pool actually does.
The pool isn’t simply a group of reporters standing inside the White House. Its rotating television crews capture professional independent video and audio and distribute that material broadly to news organizations that could not practically place separate camera crews alongside the president at every restricted event.
By Monday afternoon, a fight that began with Trump barring three news organizations had therefore expanded into a federal constitutional lawsuit, a rare unified response from competing television networks and a disruption of the independent audio and video infrastructure normally used to document presidential activities.
For the moment, Americans can still see White House-provided footage of the president.
Monday demonstrated something else:
Without the independent television pool, seeing the president and hearing what the president is saying can become two very different things.
Stay with JRL CHARTS LGBT Politics USA for continuing coverage of the White House media-access fight, the federal court challenge and its implications for press freedom in the United States.

Donald Trump made an unannounced stop in New York City on Monday evening during his two-day trip for the United Nations General Assembly, visiting Gracie Mansion on the Upper East Side to meet with Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
Following the hour-long meeting, a reporter questioned Trump about his decision to bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House and asked whether Mamdani had given him any advice.
Trump gestured toward the crowd of journalists assembled outside and replied: “They said they were going to boycott me but they never boycott me.”
He then delivered a five-word taunt: “Look at all that press!”
Trump’s remarks came only hours after a chaotic ribbon-cutting ceremony on the White House lawn. Video of the event was broadcast around the world, but there was no audio after major networks boycotted the president’s announcement of a new helipad.
The White House television pool, which includes ABC, CBS, Fox, CNN and NBC, had earlier announced that it would suspend coverage of all presidential events in solidarity with journalists who were barred by the administration over the weekend.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration on Monday morning, accusing it of violating their First Amendment rights after their reporters were denied entry to the White House.
Standing alongside Trump at the podium, Mamdani avoided endorsing the president’s criticism. “I told the president that we’re going to have all of the members of the press here on the lawn and that is something that I believe in. As everyone, no matter the opinion or the critique, that we engage,” Mamdani said.
Donald Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speak to reporters during a press conference following their meeting at Gracie Mansion in New York City, US, September 21
Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speak to reporters
Trump and Mamdani also said they had discussed a proposal that could bring about 12,000 homes and 30,000 jobs to New York. The plan could ultimately create an entirely new neighborhood on the site of a major rail yard in Sunnyside, Queens.
Mamdani said the two sides had agreed to open a new level of dialogue about developing the site, a project that would require substantial cooperation and investment.
Trump also claimed that he had helped influence Mamdani’s decision to move into Gracie Mansion.
According to Trump, the mayor had been uncertain about relocating to the “luxurious Gracie Mansion” until Trump advised him to live there.
Trump spoke favorably of Mamdani, saying the mayor “certainly got potential.”
Ahead of his arrival, Trump called the mayor’s official residence “one of his favorite places in the world” and recalled spending “lots of hours there over the years” with previous New York mayors.
“It will be interesting to see how it looks now, invited by Mayor Mamdani. Look forward to it,” Trump wrote.
The meeting marked the third face-to-face encounter between Trump and Mamdani, but it was their first meeting in New York City.
President Donald Trump, riding inside ‘The Beast,’ arriving at Gracie Mansion for a meeting with New York mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday evening
Trump described Mamdani as a ‘very rational person’ and said he could ‘surprise some conservative people,’ during their first meeting in the Oval Office back in November 2025
The two previously met at the White House in November 2025, shortly after Mamdani’s election, and again in February.
Mamdani’s communications director, Anna Bahr, said Monday’s meeting would focus on ‘issues affecting New York City and New Yorkers.’
The White House confirmed the meeting but did not provide additional details.
And the meeting marks a striking shift in a relationship that began with very public hostility toward one an other.
During Mamdani’s 2025 mayoral campaign, Trump repeatedly attacked the Democratic socialist, at one point calling him a ‘100% Communist Lunatic.’
Trump also criticized Mamdani’s political agenda and warned about the potential consequences of his policies for New York.
Mamdani, on the campaign was sharply critical of Trump and his administration, particularly over immigration enforcement.
During the campaign, he called ICE a ‘rogue agency’ and said that if Trump pursued his promised mass deportation effort in New York, he would ‘have to get through me’ to do so.’
During Mamdani’s mayoral campaign, he called ICE a ‘rogue agency’ and said that if Trump pursued his promised mass deportation effort in New York, he would ‘have to get through me’ to do so’
He also accused Trump of using the threat of federal enforcement to intimidate New Yorkers.
But the tone changed considerably after Mamdani won the election.
When the two first met in the Oval Office back in November 2025, their interaction was notably cordial.
Trump described Mamdani as a ‘very rational person’ and said he could ‘surprise some conservative people.’
Trump also said he would be happy if Mamdani succeeded in running New York.
The two met again at the White House in February, with housing among the issues discussed.
Mamdani has said the pair remain in contact by phone and text, although he has declined to discuss how frequently they communicate or what they talk about.
Trump’s visit is particularly notable because presidential visits to Gracie Mansion are rare.
The last sitting president to visit was Ronald Reagan in 1981, meaning Trump’s meeting with Mamdani marks the first presidential visit to the mayor’s residence in 45 years.
Trump’s week in New York City features high-level diplomacy, with the United Nations General Assembly bringing world leaders from across the globe to Manhattan.
The president is due to address the UN on Tuesday and is holding a string of meetings with foreign leaders, including Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi.
Talks on Iran, the Middle East and other international issues are expected to take place before Trump heads back to Washington later in the week for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House.

With three media companies now suing President Donald Trump after being banned from White House access, the federal judge handling the emergency case is one appointed by the commander in chief in his first term.
Yet the president is not happy with the random selection.
In a lengthy post on Truth Social Monday afternoon, Trump said: “As expected, Fake News CNN, Politico (Pay back the 8 Million Dollar contribution made by the U.S. Government to keep them afloat!), and MSNOW (formerly known as MSDNC!), have brought suit to gain access to the White House, and your President, ME!
“They have drawn a great Judge, for them, a man who ruled in favor of Jim Acosta, who now seems to have disappeared from the Planet. The Judge’s name is Tim Kelly, and he was, sadly, appointed by ‘TRUMP.’
“In other words, almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal because Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown ‘sources,’ shouldn’t be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World.
“It is called the Oval Office, and it should be treated with Decorum, Respect, and Dignity, not defiled by Third Rate Clowns, who purposefully distort, twist, and degrade with everything they write or publish. Virtually every story about me, or anything having to do with me, is negative, wrong and, in many cases, DANGEROUS for our Country! No matter how GREAT my Achievements, they trivialize and demean.
“The fact is, I won all seven Swing States, the Popular Vote, the Electoral College (312 to 226), and the Counties throughout America by 86%, and yet it is reported that I get 94% bad publicity. With such a Crooked and Corrupt Press, how did I win in such a LANDSLIDE? It is because the Media has NO credibility, and that is a very bad thing for our Nation!
“Why should I have to give ‘access’ to such people? Perhaps Judge Kelly could explain that! In any event, I have an obligation to fight for the Success and Safety of our Country. FAKE NEWS IS A THREAT TO DEMOCRACY, and I will do whatever is necessary to make sure that the U.S.A. thrives. MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN!”
Jacqui Heinrich on Trump banning 3 news outlets from the White House:
“While people might cheer this on, bear in mind the long reach of decisions like this.” pic.twitter.com/bKDdnl3qlH
— The Post Millennial (@TPostMillennial) September 21, 2026
Politico reports: “Kelly presided over a similar lawsuit filed by CNN in 2018, after the White House suspended the credentials of correspondent Jim Acosta following a dispute over his actions during a press conference. Kelly held a hearing on the suspension the day after the lawsuit was filed and quickly ordered the White House to restore Acosta’s press pass, citing a lack of due process for the journalist.”
“Kelly is perhaps best known for presiding over the six-month jury trial of leaders of the Proud Boys who were charged with seditious conspiracy for their role in the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol. After their convictions, Kelly sentenced the group’s national chair, Enrique Tarrio, to a 22-year prison term, the lengthiest for any Jan. 6 defendant. Kelly recently, and reluctantly, ended the Proud Boys case after the Justice Department moved to dismiss the charges in connection with Trump’s grant of clemency to all those charged with Jan. 6-related offenses.”
Meanwhile, major TV networks are standing in solidarity, declining to replace CNN’s White House pool crew.
“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting,” ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC said in a rare joint statement.
The result is that shared TV pool will not cover Trump events designated for pool coverage, according to an email Monday from Bryan Boughton, the Fox News Washington bureau chief who currently chairs the pool, reported CNN.
“This follows the White House’s position preventing CNN from fulfilling its assigned pool duties,” Boughton wrote. “There will be no replacement pool put in place.”
POTUS blocked CNN/MSNOW/Politico from the WH and now they are all suing. Fox has also jumped on the pile!
Oh the irony – Judge Tim Kelly, a Trump appointed judge, has been assigned to the case. 😂 pic.twitter.com/dwvk9HnjgE
— Diane 🇺🇸 America First (@Lowcountry1Girl) September 21, 2026
“This is to advise that, effective today, the TV pool will not be covering events designated as pool coverage of the President,” Boughton indicated.
All other TV pool coverage “will continue as normal, including Congress, VIPs, and selected events in Washington and around the country,” he added.
In an earlier post Monday, Trump denied he was attacking anyone’s First Amendment rights.
“The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish,” he explained.
“It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America. It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW! Thank you for your attention to this matter.”
🚨 LMFAO!! REPORTER: Mayor Mamdani, your response to Trump banning outlets from the White House? POTUS, are you banning them to distract?
MAMDANI: I told the President that we’re going to have all of the members of the press here on the lawn
TRUMP: They said they’d BOYCOTT me,… pic.twitter.com/F7T7rHQ7qs
